# better-npm-audit

> A CLI that wraps `npm audit` and `pnpm audit`. It lets a project accept known vulnerabilities with a reason and an expiry date, so a CI build fails only on new ones. Node.js 18 or later (version 3 for Node 14.6 - 16).

Run it in a project that has a lockfile: `npx better-npm-audit audit --json`.

- Exit code `0`: nothing unhandled at or above `--level`. Exit code `1`: unhandled vulnerabilities, or the audit could not run.
- With `--json`, stdout is one JSON document and nothing else (the table and messages go to stderr). Read `passed`, then `unhandledIds`. A failure is `{ "passed": false, "error": "..." }`.
- Accept a reviewed vulnerability in `.nsprc` (JSON or YAML) with `notes` and an `expiry`, not on the command line. `-m pkg@version` ignores a module only at that version. `--ignore-dependencies-of pkg` ignores what a package brings in.
- Auto-detects pnpm from `pnpm-lock.yaml`; use `--package-manager npm|pnpm` to choose.
